transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. As most of you know, the platform team has a replacement CI runner system based on ephemeral runners that passed our standard build-speed and failure-recovery tests in staging. Before I make a final approval decision, I want to hear from each of you — developer productivity, site reliability, and compliance — on the draft operating policy. Specifically, the policy currently allows 20 concurrent jobs, keeps build logs for 30 days, and doesn't specify immutable log storage or build-provenance attestations. I'd like to get your input on whether those settings are adequate or if we need to tighten anything up before publishing. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we go further. Yesterday, while helping the release team debug a separate build, I confirmed that the production release pipeline uses privileged Docker-in-Docker, which cannot run on the proposed ephemeral runner profile. The workable design is exactly two isolated persistent runners dedicated to release jobs, with all remaining jobs on ephemeral runners. I haven't updated the platform proposal yet, so the current draft doesn't account for this.

transcript.text: During an unrelated queue investigation this morning, I measured a campaign-day burst of 28 simultaneous CI jobs. The safe production ceiling is exactly 32 concurrent jobs, and the queue should generate an alert when it exceeds 24 jobs. For the policy, 32 is the max_concurrent_jobs value to use; 28 is only the observed burst that motivates raising the draft limit. I haven't added those measurements to the capacity dashboard yet.

transcript.text: I need to flag a compliance issue with the draft policy. This afternoon, while preparing evidence for an audit, I confirmed that build logs for our regulated release repositories must be retained for exactly 180 days in immutable storage, and each production build must produce a signed provenance attestation. The current draft's 30-day retention with no immutability or provenance attestation requirement falls well short of these requirements. I haven't opened the compliance ticket yet, but these are hard requirements we need to address before the policy can be approved.

Require signed provenance attestations for each production build

Open the compliance ticket documenting the 180-day immutable log retention and signed provenance attestation requirements for regulated release repositories
